newsitem.title: CHINA: China to double banks in open market operations.
newsitem.headline: China to double banks in open market operations.

text.p: China will more than double the number of banks permitted to take part in open market operations, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Since China's central bank, the People's Bank of China, formally launched its trial open market operations last April, 14 banks had been included, the newspaper quoted Wang Ping, executive vice-president of the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co as saying.
More than a dozen urban cooperation banks would be allowed to join, raising the number of banks authorised to take part to about 30, he said.

The company was set up last year by the central bank and the Ministry of Finance and is responsible for the custody and settlement of bonds through its electronic network linking financial institutions.

So far, more than 150 billion yuan ($18 billion) in treasury bonds, more than 300 billion yuan in policy-oriented bonds and about 80 billion yuan of central bank financing bonds have been deposited with the company.
The Ministry of Finance plans to regularly float more short-term paperless debt through the network as open market operations expand, Wang said.
China plans to issue 248.596 billion yuan of domestic and overseas debt in 1997, up by 27.3 percent from last year.
